subject: Follow-up: Confirmation of no model training & EU log handling
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@medisight.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: privacy@medisight.com
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — confirmation items

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team appreciated the walkthrough of routing and batching controls. Before we move to a technical evaluation, Legal and Privacy asked for a short written confirmation on two things we discussed verbally:

1) That Redwood will not use any MediSight customer content for model training or improvement unless explicitly agreed in writing.
2) That logs containing customer content (request/response payloads) for the EU region will be stored in EU-only storage, purged on a 30-day retention window by default, and that we can arrange stricter retention (14 days) for sensitive projects.

Can you confirm both points in writing and include any standard artifacts (SOC2 snapshot, opt-out statement) we can attach to our vendor review? Also, what redaction or PII-minimization steps do you recommend for us to implement client-side before sending data to your hosted endpoints?

Best,
Samantha Green
Head of Product Ops
MediSight Health

Attachment: discovery-notes.pdf (referenced)
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@medisight.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T11:08:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — confirmation items

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear summary. Short answers up front, followed by details and next steps.

1) Training on customer data: Confirmed — Redwood will not use MediSight customer content to train or improve our public models unless there is an explicit written agreement that authorizes that usage (e.g., a signed model-usage addendum). This includes fine-tuning, continual learning, and inclusion in model corpora.

2) EU log residency & retention: We confirm EU-only storage for requests and responses when the account is configured for EU residency. Default retention for full request/response logs for EU accounts is 30 days; for this pilot we can scope a 14-day retention policy as part of the Dedicated or Private plan.

PII minimization and redaction guidance (recommendations):
- Client-side hashing of direct identifiers (email, SSNs) before transmission when possible.
- Remove or tokenise patient identifiers if exact values are not needed for the use case.
- For structured health records, use field-level allowlists rather than free-text ingestion.
- Use our prefix-trimming option to avoid sending long patient notes that contain unrelated PHI.

Operational controls we provide:
- KV cache scoping: keys and cache snapshots are isolated per customer and not exported to model training.
- No internal human review: by default, customer payloads are not surfaced for model improvement review.
- Audit logs: admin-level audit entries show access and retention operations (we provided a SOC2 artifact attached).

Attached I am sending: a one-page draft opt-out statement you can include in your vendor packet (redwood-optout-statement-draft.pdf) and a SOC2 snapshot (soc2-snapshot-2027.pdf). Laura (Legal) and Marissa (AE) are looped for any contractual follow-up.

Next steps
- If you want the 14-day retention option, confirm on this thread and we'll generate a scoped order + config doc.
- If your privacy team wants additional redaction tooling, we can share a short pre-send sanitization checklist and a sample Lambda for client-side hashing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with Privacy if helpful.

— Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-1298

Attachments: redwood-optout-statement-draft.pdf; soc2-snapshot-2027.pdf; initial-discovery-qa.docx
From: privacy@medisight.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha.green@medisight.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-15T15:33:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — confirmation items

Logan / Redwood team —

Thank you for the prompt reply and the artifacts. A couple of clarifying points from Privacy:
- The 30 -> 14 day retention reduction needs to be enforced and auditable. Please confirm the deletion job cadence and that deletion events are recorded in audit logs with timestamp and operator id.
- For EU-only storage, confirm that backups and replicas are likewise stored in-region and that cross-region failover would not copy logs out of EU without explicit change control.
- Please confirm there will be no use of this content for synthetic example generation or internal model validation.

If you can provide the deletion audit sample and the backup/replica statement, we can proceed to a short vendor approval.

Regards,
Marta Novak
Privacy Counsel
MediSight Health
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: privacy@medisight.com, Samantha Green <samantha.green@medisight.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-16T10:04:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — confirmation items

Marta / Samantha —

Thanks — below are the specific confirmations you requested (I’ve kept them short for inclusion in your vendor packet). Legal can turn these into contract language if you like.

1) Deletion job and audit events
- Deletion cadence: Retention deletions run nightly for EU log buckets; targeted retention (`14-day`) starts from object creation timestamp and deletes eligible objects in the first nightly job after day 14.
- Audit events: Each deletion operation writes an audit record (object id, timestamp, initiating-system id) to an append-only audit table; a summarized deletion report (CSV) is available for account admins on request.

2) Backups / replicas / failover
- Backups and replicas for EU-resident accounts remain in EU regions (primary + hot replica in the same legal region). Cross-region replication is disabled for EU-resident log buckets unless explicitly enabled via change control and customer consent.

3) No training / no internal generation
- Confirmed in writing: Customer data will not be used to train, validate, or generate synthetic training sets for our public or internal models unless a signed addendum to the Master Services Agreement explicitly opt-ins to that activity. This includes human-in-the-loop labeling programs.

Attached: redwood-optout-statement-draft.pdf (signed-by-default placeholder), soc2-snapshot-2027.pdf.

If that covers your audit needs, we will prepare a short order amendment to lock the 14-day retention and EU-residency settings for the pilot environment. Marissa, Laura — can you prepare the scoped amendment and a DSAR/retention SLA appendix?

Happy to join the vendor call next week to confirm.

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
